title: Six Norwegian forest cats in my game, and trying to get the breed right
author: Brave-History-6502
selftext:
Fjordfall is a free browser game set in a Norway-inspired valley, which I started after a trip there and have been building with my kids. There are six Norwegian forest cats in it now, and I wanted them to be the breed rather than generic cats.

A bit about the breed, since that's what I built toward: norsk skogkatt has a thick double coat that sheds rain and snow, a full ruff at the neck and a long bushy tail, and they're slow to grow up (often three to five years). They were nearly lost last century until Norwegian breeders brought them back.

In the game the coat is fur rather than a painted texture: long on the ruff, the britches and the tail, short on the face and paws, and it moves in the wind. The colours are ones the breed comes in: a red-and-white tom, a blue-grey, a black-and-white, a brown tabby, an odd-eyed white and a tortoiseshell.

Each one lives somewhere (a summer farm, a churchyard gate by the fjord, a harbour, a seter) and keeps a day on a clock shared by everyone playing: the meadow in the morning, the trail post, the door in the evening. They lie out in the sun on clear days, keep to the door when it's wet, and sleep at night. You earn their trust slowly, with a hand and then a treat, and the shy ones keep their distance until they know you. In spring the tortoiseshell has kittens that follow her around in a line.

How they were made, since this is r/aigamedev: the body and head started as Meshy generations from multi-view images, and each cat's coat is a Meshy retexture of that model. Meshy sculpts fur as thin flaps, which tear when you skin them, so a Blender Python recipe (written with Claude Code) rebuilds it into one clean rigged body, bakes each coat onto it, and solves the walk, trot, sit, loaf, stretch and leap clips frame by frame from targets for the paws, pelvis and head. The fur you see is a shell shader in three.js that the wind moves. Most of the iteration was me looking at them in the game and asking for changes ("the face really needs work", "even bigger").

If you just want to meet one, there's a small page that shows today's cat for thirty seconds: [https://fjordfall.fly.dev/katter.html](https://fjordfall.fly.dev/katter.html)

The game, where you can find all six: [https://fjordfall.fly.dev/?via=ragd](https://fjordfall.fly.dev/?via=ragd)

Still early. The video is 22 seconds from the game itself.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: Tried to play, couldn't, You need to some performance tuning.

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: it’s a large world so takes a bit for everything to load in, I have spent a few cycles on optimizing but needs some more tweaks

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: What device if you don’t mind me asking?

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: it does take a 30-60 seconds — I probably need to figure out how to make it even faster-/ but it is a fairly large game/world.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body: It loaded when I was in, it was really laggy, do you have analytics setup?

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body:
Yeah, custom analytics but do try and track time to first interaction for all users, FPS, and a few other things -- the problem is I think I'm letting people start the game too early so the world is still loading in, and FPS is terrible.

The models over optimized for the game starting ASAP I think.

Thanks for giving it a try -- will work on getting the start up smoother!

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: Give it another try when you have a chance -- It should be a bit faster/smoother hopefully.
